title: Festive Fare: Mixed Dips and Crostini.
subtitle: Made to share – take a plate or dine in!
description: Make it an Australian festive season to remember with our selection of celebration finger food. Serve up two delicious dips – caramelised onion and dill, and Middle Eastern white bean – and get the party started!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C. Line 2 oven trays with baking paper. Peel the carrot and halve lengthwise, then cut into 1cm chunks. Thinly slice the onion. Finely chop the dill, discarding the stems. Combine half the cumin and coriander spice blend, 2 tsp olive oil and 1 tsp red wine vinegar in a large bowl, then season with salt and pepper.

Roast carrot and beans: Put the carrot on a lined tray, drizzle with 2 tsp of the cumin mixture and toss to coat. Roast for 10 mins. Meanwhile, drain and rinse half the beans. Toss the beans in the remaining cumin mixture, then add to the tray with the carrot and spread in a single layer. Roast for a further 10 mins or until the beans are warmed through and the carrot is tender.

Bake crostini: Cut the baguettes on an angle into 1cm-thick slices (see Make it yours) and put on the remaining lined tray. Spray or brush both sides with olive oil. Bake, turning over halfway, for 10-12 mins until crisp and golden. Meanwhile, heat 1 tbs olive oil in a medium frypan over medium heat. Cook the onion, stirring regularly, for 5-6 mins until softened.

Caramelise onion: Add 2 tbs red wine vinegar and 1 tbs sugar to the onion. Reduce the heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, for 3-4 mins until caramelised. Remove the pan from the heat. Meanwhile, put the cream cheese in a bowl and stir with a wooden spoon until smooth. Stir in the caramelised onion and dill.

Serve up: Put the carrot and beans in a separate bowl, add 1 tbs olive oil and 1 tsp red wine vinegar and blend until smooth. Taste both dips and season with salt and pepper, then transfer to two serving bowls. Put the crostini and dips on a serving platter and enjoy! Serves 4.
Make it yours: Fancy long crostini? Cut the baguettes into thirds lengthwise instead, or do a mix of the two like we have.
